thread:
Miriam K: Hey team — quick question. I booked a cheap non-refundable flight for a client trip, but my visa was delayed so I had to change to a refundable fare and pay the fare difference + the airline change fee on my personal card. Can I get reimbursed for both? Booking ref: ABC123. Receipts attached.
Jordan (People Ops): Hi @Miriam K — sorry that happened. Can you confirm: did you request pre-approval before upgrading the fare, or was this an emergency? :thinking_face:
Miriam K: No pre-approval, it was same-day when embassy emailed the delay. I have the embassy email saying date moved + the new e-ticket and change fee receipt. Total difference was $420. Airline charged $85 change fee.
Finance Bot: Policy note: Per travel policy, fare upgrades due to visa/delay are reimbursable if accompanied by evidence (visa delay email) and manager approval in the expense comment. Any out-of-policy items will be reviewed case-by-case.
Darren L: I approve this — Miriam, can you add a short note in the expense: "Manager approval: Darren L — visa delay" and attach the embassy email thread? :white_check_mark:
Miriam K: Thanks!! I'll upload receipts. Do I pick "Flight — fare difference" or "Change fee" separate categories in Expensify?
Elena - Travel Admin: Hi — for our ledger, please do two line items: 1) Flight fare difference (category: Travel - Airfare) 2) Change fee (category: Travel - Fees). Upload both receipts and the visa delay proof. If you paid on personal card, mark payment method as "Personal Card" and add the manager approval in comments.
Travel Desk (Amelia): Also worth noting: if you had an existing company-approved booking and travel desk could have rebooked, we usually ask team to route changes through travel@redwood.com — but we can make exceptions for embassy/visa timing issues. We'll flag internal travel desk notes to avoid duplicate charges.
Miriam K: Got it. One more thing — the difference was charged in EUR (EUR 380) and change fee USD 85. How should I report currency?
Finance Bot: Report amounts in original currency and attach the card statement showing the exchange. Expensify will convert, but include a brief note: "EUR 380 = USD XXX (card rate)". If you need help with conversion, attach the statement and Finance will use the card's posted conversion rate.
Jordan (People Ops): For expediency, tag this as "urgent" in the expense report and set a follow-up with Finance. Since Darren approved, it should process normally. If total reimbursement (converted) exceeds $500, it will trigger manual review — Finance Bot will mention if so.
Miriam K: Uploaded: 1) embassy_email.pdf 2) e-ticket_new.pdf 3) airline_change_receipt.jpg 4) personal_card_statement.png. Filed expense with comment "Manager approval: Darren L — visa delay" and tagged urgent.
Finance Bot: Received. Automated check: total converted = $520 — manual review required. @Jordan (People Ops) please confirm manager approval exists in thread (it does). Finance will queue this under manual approvals queue.
Jordan (People Ops): Confirmed, manager approval present. I'll add a short attestation in the expense: "People Ops confirms exceptional visa-related rebook approved by manager."
Finance Bot: OK queued. Expected turnaround for manual approvals ~ 3 business days. If any item is denied, you'll get an explanation and next steps.
Miriam K: Appreciate it. One last Q: any tax/VAT reclaim on the EUR fare difference? The airline ticket shows VAT on their invoice.
Elena - Travel Admin: If VAT is itemized and recoverable, Finance will attempt reclaim for company expenses. Personal card purchases normally aren't reclaimed for VAT back to the employee — we'll process VAT reclaim as a company reimbursement if eligible. Attach the airline invoice with VAT breakdown.
Darren L: Thanks team. Miriam — please ping me if Finance pushes back and I'll escalate.
Miriam K: Will do. Thanks everyone :pray:
